title: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Curriculum Framework (0096) — Stage 3
version: Version 1.1; published September 2020 for first teaching September 2021
notes: Pelengkap cambridge-primary-maths.json (Stage 1–2 + TWM): semua learning objective Stage 3 (hlm. 21–23), dibaca dari teks PDF yang sama dengan PyMuPDF dan diperiksa manual.
Sub-butir (o) di 3Ss.02 digabung dipisah ';' seperti konvensi berkas Stage 1–2. Selain itu teks verbatim.
Dibuat agen MAT SD1–SD3, 25 Okt 2026; berkas lama tidak disunting.

entries.text: Estimate the number of objects or people (up to 1000).
Count on and count back in steps of constant size: 1-digit numbers, tens or hundreds, starting from any number (from 0 to 1000).
Use knowledge of even and odd numbers up to 10 to recognise and sort numbers.
Recognise the use of an object to represent an unknown quantity in addition and subtraction calculations.
Recognise and extend linear sequences, and describe the term-to-term rule.
Extend spatial patterns formed from adding and subtracting a constant.
Recite, read and write number names and whole numbers (from 0 to 1000).
Understand the commutative and associative properties of addition, and use these to simplify calculations.
Recognise complements of 100 and complements of multiples of 10 or 100 (up to 1000).
Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers with up to three digits (regrouping of ones or tens).
Understand and explain the relationship between multiplication and division.
Understand and explain the commutative and distributive properties of multiplication, and use these to simplify calculations.
Know 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 times tables.
Estimate and multiply whole numbers up to 100 by 2, 3, 4 and 5.
Estimate and divide whole numbers up to 100 by 2, 3, 4 and 5.
Recognise multiples of 2, 5 and 10 (up to 1000).
Interpret money notation for currencies that use a decimal point.
Add and subtract amounts of money to give change.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Understand and explain that the value of each digit is determined by its position in that number (up to 3-digit numbers).

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Use knowledge of place value to multiply whole numbers by 10.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Compose, decompose and regroup 3-digit numbers, using hundreds, tens and ones.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Understand the relative size of quantities to compare and order 3-digit positive numbers, using the symbols =, > and <.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Round 3-digit numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand and explain that fractions are several equal parts of an object or shape and all the parts, taken together, equal one whole.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that the relationship between the whole and the parts depends on the relative size of each, regardless of their shape or orientation.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand and explain that fractions can describe equal parts of a quantity or set of objects.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that a fraction can be represented as a division of the numerator by the denominator (half, quarter and three-quarters).

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that fractions (half, quarter, three-quarters, third and tenth) can act as operators.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Recognise that two fractions can have an equivalent value (halves, quarters, fifths and tenths).

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Estimate, add and subtract fractions with the same denominator (within one whole).

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Use knowledge of equivalence to compare and order unit fractions and fractions with the same denominator, using the symbols =, > and <.
Choose the appropriate unit of time for familiar activities.
Read and record time accurately in digital notation (12-hour) and on analogue clocks.
Interpret and use the information in timetables (12-hour clock).
Understand the difference between a time and a time interval. Find time intervals between the same units in days, weeks, months and years.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify, describe, classify, name and sketch 2D shapes by their properties. Differentiate between regular and irregular polygons.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Estimate and measure lengths in centimetres (cm), metres (m) and kilometres (km). Understand the relationship between units.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand that perimeter is the total distance around a 2D shape and can be calculated by adding lengths, and area is how much space a 2D shape occupies within its boundary.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Draw lines, rectangles and squares. Estimate, measure and calculate the perimeter of a shape, using appropriate metric units, and area on a square grid.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify, describe, sort, name and sketch 3D shapes by their properties.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Estimate and measure the mass of objects in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). Understand the relationship between units.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Estimate and measure capacity in millilitres (ml) and litres (l), and understand their relationships.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Recognise pictures, drawings and diagrams of 3D shapes.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry on 2D shapes and patterns.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Compare angles with a right angle. Recognise that a straight line is equivalent to two right angles or a half turn.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Use instruments that measure length, mass, capacity and temperature.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Position and transformation
entries.text: Interpret and create descriptions of position, direction and movement, including reference to cardinal points.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Position and transformation
entries.text: Sketch the reflection of a 2D shape in a horizontal or vertical mirror line, including where the mirror line is the edge of the shape.
Conduct an investigation to answer non-statistical and statistical questions (categorical and discrete data).

Record, organise and represent categorical and discrete data. Choose and explain which representation to use in a given situation: Venn and Carroll diagrams; tally charts and frequency tables; pictograms and bar charts.
Interpret data, identifying similarities and variations, within data sets, to answer non-statistical and statistical questions and discuss conclusions.
Use familiar language associated with chance to describe events, including ‘it will happen’, ‘it will not happen’, ‘it might happen’.
Conduct chance experiments, and present and describe the results.
